links.outcome: Readability of LLM responses to IBS patient questions
links.effect: Both LLMs produced difficult-to-read content; Gemini FRE 35.83 ± 3.31 vs ChatGPT 32.33 ± 5.57 (p = 0.21), corresponding to college-level proficiency.
links.quote: Readability analysis showed both LLMs generated difficult-to-read content: Gemini's FRE score was 35.83 ± 3.31 vs. ChatGPT's 32.33 ± 5.57 (p = 0.21), corresponding to college-level proficiency.

links.outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated patient education content
links.effect: Both models' outputs required college-level proficiency (FRE 35.83 Gemini, 32.33 ChatGPT), above typical patient reading levels.

links.outcome: Comprehensiveness and accuracy of LLM answers to IBS FAQs, including outdated content
links.effect: Gemini comprehensive and accurate for 94.9% (37/39), ChatGPT 89.7% (35/39); mixed responses were vague or outdated; no significant difference (p = 0.67).
links.quote: Gemini produced comprehensive and accurate answers for 94.9% (37/39) of questions, with two rated as mixed (vague/outdated).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation benchmarking the accuracy, readability, and empathy of ChatGPT-4 and Gemini-1 on frequently asked questions about irritable bowel syndrome without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
